The sky appears blue because sunlight, which is made of all colors of the visible spectrum, interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere through a process called **Rayleigh scattering**.

Sunlight consists of all colors of the visible spectrum. When these rays hit our atmosphere, shorter wavelengths (blue and violet light) are scattered much more strongly than longer-wavelength colors like red or yellow because they interact more frequently with air molecules. While we see the sky as blue rather than a mix of all colors, it is actually a combination of all visible wavelengths scattering off gas molecules; our eyes simply perceive the combined effect of these scattered wavelengths as a pale blue sky. The sun appears white because our eyes adapt to the mixture of all these scattered wavelengths, making the sky appear blue or white depending on the time of day and atmospheric conditions.
